title: Synthetic: UHD rejected on L3 Android TV lab profile
content: Symptom: UHD asset played on desktop Chrome but produced video failure on an Android TV test profile. Evidence: TV CDM reported L3; UHD policy required L1; 1080p fallback was allowed. Root cause: device robustness did not meet the UHD license policy. Confirmation: the same asset worked on an L1 device and the L3 profile played the allowed lower tier.

title: Synthetic: AVR reduced HDCP path below UHD requirement
content: Symptom: UHD playback showed audio with black video through a receiver but worked when connected directly to the display. Evidence: output-restricted key status and HDCP 1.4 through the receiver; policy required 2.2. Root cause: display-chain HDCP downgrade. Confirmation: direct connection reported HDCP 2.2 and restored video.

title: Synthetic: HEVC Main10 selected on unsupported decoder
content: Symptom: license acquisition succeeded but video decoder initialization failed on one TV generation. Evidence: selected rendition was HEVC Main10; device capability data did not include the required secure Main10 decoder. Root cause: codec/profile incompatibility. Confirmation: forced AVC rendition played successfully.

title: Synthetic: expired entitlement token caused license 403
content: Symptom: encrypted streams failed while clear streams worked. Evidence: license endpoint returned 403 and server request ID mapped to token expiry. Root cause: stale entitlement token cached by the client. Confirmation: token refresh produced a successful and usable license.

title: Synthetic: manifest default_KID did not match packaged track
content: Symptom: license HTTP response was 200 but CDM reported no usable key. Evidence: MPD default_KID differed from the encrypted track KID and license database record. Root cause: stale manifest after repackaging. Confirmation: publishing the matching MPD restored playback.

title: Synthetic: regional CDN token omitted from segment requests
content: Symptom: startup failed in one region after manifest and license succeeded. Evidence: first video segment returned 403; signed query parameter was lost on redirected segment requests. Root cause: player/CDN redirect integration. Confirmation: preserving the signed query string restored segment delivery.

title: Synthetic: Widevine policy investigation on Android TV lab
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: Android TV lab. Symptom: L3 device requested an L1-only UHD tier. Evidence: CDM reported L3 and HD fallback worked. Root cause: robustness policy mismatch. Confirmation: verify the title on an L1 reference device.

title: Synthetic: HDCP investigation on web reference player
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: web reference player. Symptom: protected video became black on an external display path. Evidence: output-restricted status appeared after route change. Root cause: display chain negotiated below policy. Confirmation: connect directly to a known HDCP 2.2 display.

title: Synthetic: Codec investigation on smart-TV QA rack
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: smart-TV QA rack. Symptom: audio played while video decoder creation failed. Evidence: selected representation required an unsupported secure profile. Root cause: codec and secure-decoder incompatibility. Confirmation: force the AVC compatibility rendition.

title: Synthetic: License investigation on set-top-box staging
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: set-top-box staging. Symptom: encrypted playback failed while clear playback succeeded. Evidence: license endpoint returned 403 with an expired entitlement. Root cause: authorization token expiry. Confirmation: refresh entitlement and correlate the request ID.

title: Synthetic: CENC/PSSH investigation on Android TV lab
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: Android TV lab. Symptom: license returned successfully but no key became usable. Evidence: manifest KID and encrypted track KID differed. Root cause: stale packaging metadata. Confirmation: inspect PSSH and tenc KIDs together.

title: Synthetic: CDN investigation on web reference player
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: web reference player. Symptom: startup failed after manifest and license success. Evidence: first video segment returned 403 at one edge. Root cause: signed media URL was lost during redirect. Confirmation: preserve query parameters through redirects.

title: Synthetic: HLS investigation on smart-TV QA rack
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: smart-TV QA rack. Symptom: live playback stalled at a discontinuity. Evidence: media sequence advanced without matching discontinuity state. Root cause: playlist continuity error. Confirmation: validate sequence values across origin and edge.

title: Synthetic: MPEG-DASH investigation on set-top-box staging
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: set-top-box staging. Symptom: live playback repeatedly jumped behind the live edge. Evidence: client clock differed from MPD timing by several seconds. Root cause: clock synchronization error. Confirmation: synchronize UTC timing and replay.

title: Synthetic: FairPlay investigation on Android TV lab
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: Android TV lab. Symptom: SPC generation succeeded but CKC processing failed. Evidence: wrong environment certificate was selected. Root cause: FairPlay certificate mismatch. Confirmation: repeat with the matching application certificate.

title: Synthetic: PlayReady investigation on web reference player
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: web reference player. Symptom: UHD license processed but output stayed restricted. Evidence: license OPL exceeded the active display path. Root cause: PlayReady output protection policy. Confirmation: test an allowed HD tier on the same client.

title: Synthetic: ABR investigation on smart-TV QA rack
content: Synthetic QA scenario. Environment: smart-TV QA rack. Symptom: player oscillated between renditions and rebuffered. Evidence: short throughput samples overestimated available bandwidth. Root cause: unstable ABR estimation. Confirmation: pin a sustainable representation and compare buffer health.
